deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 13-16): Grothendieck is listing the elementary operations on the objects of his 'topological Teichmüller groupoids'. The objects are compact oriented surfaces with boundary circles C_a, some of them 'marked' (C ∩ R ≠ ∅, i.e. carrying a marked point, which rigidifies the circle); on the next page they also carry orbifold weights r(a). He encodes them by weighted graphs: vertices are pieces, edges are cutting circles, and free edges (A_ℓ) are boundary circles. The operations are: (B) 'gommer', erasing a circle by contracting it to a point; (C) 'découpage', cutting along a family Σ' of circles, which in graph language cuts an edge at its midpoint into two free edges; and (D) 'recollement', gluing.

Lines 1-8 finish (C). For the purpose of translating the topological Teichmüller groupoids, the only structures that will occur are those whose cutting circles are effectively marked. Nevertheless one is still allowed to 'erase' or forget these markings midway, if they are indeed present. A struck-out line had begun to name the groupoid Ŝ(T)^±_top.

Lines 9 onward begin (D). Gluing is called 'the most essential, the least tautological perhaps' of all the operations. The data required are:
(a) a subset A' ⊂ A_ℓ of free edges with a fixed-point-free involution σ, i.e. a partition of A' into 2-element orbits;
(b) for each orbit {1,2}, orientation-reversing isomorphisms C_1 → C_2 and C_2 → C_1, inverse to each other.
For the result to be well determined, the isomorphism must be unique (up to isotopy). The next page shows this forces A' ⊂ A^+, i.e. the glued circles must be marked. In the orbifold setting it also forces r(a) = r(σ(a)) and the use of the contracted product R_a ∧_{Z/r} R_{a'} of the Z/rZ-torsors. In graph terms, gluing reattaches pairs of free edges end to end.

In modern terms this is the clutching/gluing structure that makes the tower of Teichmüller (mapping-class) groupoids of surfaces with marked boundary a modular-operad-like object: the 'Lego' of the Esquisse d'un programme. It is written in the half-edge-with-involution language of stable graphs.
errors: No mathematical error. One small gap: 'isomorphism unique' must mean unique up to isotopy, or unique among isomorphisms preserving the marked points. An orientation-reversing homeomorphism of circles is never literally unique. Even with marked points it is unique only up to isotopy, which is what the groupoid setting needs. The next page supplies the marking condition A' ⊂ A^+.

ideas.what: Gluing ('recollement') as the essential, non-tautological operation on surfaces with boundary. Data: a fixed-point-free involution on a set of free boundary circles plus mutually inverse orientation-reversing identifications.
ideas.modern_name: Clutching/gluing maps; modular operad structure on moduli/Teichmüller spaces; Lego of the Teichmüller tower
ideas.usually_credited_to: Knudsen (clutching morphisms, 1983); Getzler–Kapranov (modular operads, 1998); Grothendieck, Esquisse d'un programme (1984), for the Lego idea
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), Teichmüller tower / Lego sections, qualitatively; the formal data here are not given there

ideas.what: Graph encoding: cutting an edge at its midpoint gives two free edges; gluing pairs free edges via an involution.
ideas.modern_name: Stable graphs as flags/half-edges with an involution (fixed points = legs)

ideas.what: Gluing is well defined only along marked (rigidified) boundary circles. Unmarked circles may be erased midway.
ideas.modern_name: Surfaces with marked points on boundary circles / framed boundary; tangential base points

missed.claim: Grothendieck formalizes gluing in the Teichmüller groupoid tower with exactly the data later used in the half-edge (flag + involution) formalism of modular operads. He insists the glued circles be marked, which is the rigidification later used by Bakalov–Kirillov. Combined with the next page (equal orbifold indices r(a) = r(a'), contracted product of Z/r torsors), this anticipates twisted/balanced gluing at orbifold nodes as in Abramovich–Vistoli twisted curves. The link is foreshadowed in the Esquisse, so it is a matter of precise priority detail rather than a new result.
missed.quote: D) Opérations de recollement. C'est la plus essentielle, la moins tautologique peut-être de toutes les opérations
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents that Grothendieck had, in 1983, a precise operadic gluing formalism for (orbifold) Teichmüller groupoids with marked boundary. This is of historical interest for the genealogy of modular operads and the Lego-Teichmüller game, but not mathematically new.

deep.surprise_reason: A careful but standard definition of gluing data, essentially the modular-operad half-edge formalism. It is notable as an early precise formulation, but its substance is known and the Lego idea appears in the Esquisse.
transcription_corrections: Line 3: 'les cartes et diagrammes [?] ... effectivement marqués' reads in the image as 'les cercles de découpage effectivement marqués'.
Superscript 'Niveaux en... [?]' is more plausibly 'Néanmoins on'.
Struck-out line: 'par Ŝ(T)^±_top le groupoïde' (the symbol is S(T)^± with subscript top).
's'ils y tient bel et bien' is more plausibly 's'ils y sont bel et bien'.
'il faut connaître deux [?] problèmes main' is probably 'il faut comme données préliminaires' (word split 'prélimi-/naires').
'Pour que l'opération soit bien déterminée : isom. unique' continues onto p.16 ('pris dans la catégorie orbifoldique S(T)^±_top').
